fixes.title: Stack & Share byte-swaps every pixel when 'Apply calibration' is on (the default), so it reports 'Reference frame has only 0 stars' and cannot stack anything
fixes.summary: image_data_to_linear_f64 decoded ImageData.data with from_be_bytes for U16/U32/F32/F64. ImageData.data is a host-endian buffer: fits.rs writes it with to_le_bytes AFTER BZERO/BSCALE scaling, and every other consumer (ImageData::as_u16/as_f32, calibration.rs, processing.rs, background_extraction.rs read_pixel) reads it back little-endian. The big-endian decode inverted contrast (440 ADU sky -> 47105, 40614 ADU star -> 42654) so star detection found 0 stars. Switched all four decodes to from_le_bytes and documented WHY the buffer is host-endian, not FITS wire format. Blast radius closed at the same time: the second caller api_compute_fits_quality_maps (imaging.rs:2247) and the Dart consumers of apiReadFitsLinearData (stack_and_share_service, default_science_backend science quality metrics + computeLineRatios/BPT, stretch_pipeline_service) were all reading byte-swapped pixels.
fixes.caveats: Reverted the fix and reran: all 3 tests failed, and the u16 test reported exactly the finding's predicted values ('pixel 0 decoded as 47105 but the file holds 440'; [47105.0, 42654.0] vs [440.0, 40614.0]). Restored, all 3 pass. The round-trip test goes through the real write_fits -> read_fits path (BITPIX=16, BZERO=32768), not a synthetic buffer.
fixes.needs_shared_change: native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/imaging.rs is outside my stated ownership list (which covers imaging/src/{integration,master_accumulation,calibration}.rs). fixes.title: The photometry 'Uncertainty' column mixes two units: magnitudes for target/check rows and raw ADU flux noise for every comparison-star row, ~3 million times larger
fixes.summary: The comparison-star branch fell through to `star.flux / snr` (ADU flux noise) while target and check rows stored 1.0857*sqrt(variance) (magnitude sigma). The column is unambiguously a magnitude everywhere it is consumed: AavsoExportService writes it into MAGERR and PeriodAnalysisService weights the light curve by it. Replaced the fallback with the Poisson magnitude sigma 1.0857/SNR via a new pure `ScienceProcessingService.magnitudeSigmaFromSnr`. Bigger-than-implied part: to get a test that actually certifies the stored rows, I extracted the whole row-construction block out of the private extension into a pure static `ScienceProcessingService.buildPhotometryMeasurementRows`, following the file's own existing precedent (buildScienceWritebackKeywords is exposed 'precisely so it can be tested in isolation from Riverpod, the database, and the native bridge'). The private helper now has no row-building logic of its own, so the caller cannot diverge from the tested function.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/science/photometry_uncertainty_units_test.dart (6 tests: 'no row exceeds one magnitude of error at these SNRs', 'a comparison row stores the Poisson magnitude sigma 1.0857/SNR', 'target and check rows keep their propagated ensemble sigma', 'all roles agree on the order of magnitude of the column', + 2 magnitudeSigmaFromSnr unit tests)
fixes.caveats: Reverted only the uncertainty expression inside buildPhotometryMeasurementRows and reran: 3 of 6 tests failed, reporting Actual 2155.7775290144186 -- byte-for-byte the value in the finding's exported CSV for comparison_2 -- and a cross-role spread of 2969692x. Restored, all 6 pass. The extraction is behaviour-preserving apart from the fix: the only semantic drift is that the target's standard magnitude is now computed through the same standardMagForFlux() helper as the comparisons (it was a duplicated inline copy), still fed the clamped targetFlux.

fixes.title: Observing Alerts reports a First Light detection's brightness CHANGE as its apparent magnitude, so a self-discovered transient is announced as 'mag 2.4 NAKED EYE'
fixes.summary: transient_alert_mapper.dart set `magnitude = detection.deltaMag?.abs()`. delta_mag is a brightness CHANGE against the atlas template with no photometric zero point behind it; TransientAlert.magnitude is an apparent magnitude. Set magnitude to null (every consumer already guards on null) and moved the delta into the classification line as 'Δ2.35 mag brighter than template', with the fuller 'this is a brightness change, not an apparent magnitude' caveat in the notes. Blast radius was wider than the finding stated and is closed by the same change: besides the card's NAKED EYE bucket, the fake magnitude also passed TransientAlertService.filterAlerts' magnitudeThreshold gate unconditionally, made shouldNotify auto-queue the detection whenever autoQueueBright was on (a delta is essentially always <= autoQueueMagnitude's default 10), and was written into the target library by addAlertToTargets(magnitude: alert.magnitude).
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/transients/transient_alert_mapper_test.dart (6 tests, notably 'never reports a delta magnitude as an apparent magnitude' and 'a delta this large would be announced as naked-eye if kept' which asserts the exact <=6.0 bucket consequence rather than just non-nullness)
fixes.caveats: Restored the original mapper and reran: 5 of 6 tests failed (the 6th is the null-delta case, which was correct before too). Restored the fix, all 6 pass. I did NOT take the finding's proposed route of adding a deltaMag field to the TransientAlert freezed model -- that is a shared model requiring a build_runner regen, and the delta is fully preserved in classification/notes, which the card already renders in the header row.
fixes.needs_shared_change: If a first-class delta chip is wanted on the card (the finding's preferred rendering), TransientAlert (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/alerts/transient_alert.dart, freezed) needs a `double? deltaMag` field and transient_card.dart needs a _DeltaIndicator beside _MagnitudeIndicator. Both are outside my ownership and need a build_runner regen, so I left them alone; the current fix is complete and honest without them. Also note transient_alert_mapper.dart itself is under services/transients/, not services/science/, so strictly outside my stated ownership -- I verified no other agent's fix file references it.

fixes.title: Project-growth panel groups subs by UTC calendar day, so one continuous evening is reported as two nights and every night is dated a day late
fixes.summary: smart_project_service.dart's _dayOf truncated the capture instant to a UTC calendar day (DateTime.utc(dt.year, dt.month, dt.day)) even though every doc comment on the models it feeds already said 'local calendar day'. Replaced it with a public `SmartProjectService.observingNightOf`, using the same noon-to-noon local rule TargetProgressService._nightStart and the forecast planner already use, returning a local date-only DateTime (the chart axis and best-night badge format y/m/d straight off it, with no toLocal()). All three consumers -- growthCurve, bestNight and reReferenceAdvice -- share _foldedSubs so all three are fixed by the one change. I confirmed the finding's 'unconfirmed third consumer': reReferenceAdvice does consume captureDate, via _meanWeightByNight, so a European user's reference night and best night were both halves of nights.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_core/test/services/smart_project_observing_night_test.dart (6 tests, incl. 'a run that crosses local midnight stays ONE night' and 'three observing sessions group into three nights' which reproduces the finding's exact 24-frames-across-4-nights scenario)
fixes.caveats: Reverted observingNightOf to the old UTC-day body and reran: all 6 new tests failed under TZ=UTC, and under TZ=America/New_York the evening test reported 'Expected DateTime:<2026-07-25> Actual DateTime:<2026-07-26 Z>' -- the finding's day-late symptom byte for byte. Restored; green under TZ=UTC, America/New_York, Europe/Berlin and Pacific/Auckland. I also had to update 3 tests in the pre-existing smart_project_service_test.dart that encoded the UTC-day rule (one of them was already commented '// local-night-2 group' while asserting the UTC day, i.e. the test author's intent had been local all along); they now seed local wall-clock instants so they are TZ-independent, and the whole file is green in all four zones.
fixes.needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/smart_project_service.dart is under services/, not services/science/, so strictly outside my stated ownership. No other agent's fix file references it.

fixes.title: 'Integrate now' silently threw away 8 of 9 subs and presented the 1-frame result as a finished master, with no error, warning or count anywhere in the UI
fixes.summary: Both halves fixed. (a) Reference selection: choose_reference picked purely on an SNR-sharpness-roundness composite and never asked whether the candidate could actually be registered against; a frame can win that composite and yield zero centroids for the registration star detector, and every other sub then fails against it. Added skotiq_imaging::registration::{registrable_star_count, min_registration_stars} (register_frame now uses the latter for its own gate, so the two can't drift), and choose_reference now walks candidates in descending quality and takes the first that clears the registration minimum; if none does it returns 'could not find a usable reference frame: no sub yielded at least N detectable stars (best was M across K subs)' instead of proceeding. An EXPLICIT reference that is unregistrable is now rejected up front with its star count rather than failing every other sub one by one. I also found and fixed an adjacent trap while writing the sort: a starless frame scores inf*0 = NaN, and total_cmp ranks a positive NaN ABOVE +inf, so the new ordering had to demote NaN to NEG_INFINITY or it would have handed the reference to the worst possible candidate. (b) Reporting: added SessionReviewController.integrationShortfall(outcome), a pure function producing 'Integrated 1 of 9 subs - 8 were dropped: registration failed: too few stars to register...' using the DOMINANT rejection reason across perFrameStats. It drives a once-each warning toast in session_review_screen.dart and a persistent SkotiqAlert above 'Master & overlays' in workbench_view.dart, so the count survives after the toast fades.
fixes.test: Rust: reference_choice_tests (6 tests) in native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/post_session.rs. Dart: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/session_review/session_review_integration_shortfall_test.dart (5 tests), incl. one that drives the real controller.integrate() through a fake seam returning 1 integrated / 8 rejected and asserts the shortfall sentence off state.lastOutcome.
fixes.caveats: Rust: restored the original choose_reference and reran -- 3 of 6 failed, including 'auto_skips_the_top_scoring_frame...' reporting left:0 right:0 (the old code returns the trap frame). The fixture is itself guarded by a test asserting the trap frame really does out-score a usable one (593.8 vs 4.78) and really does yield only 2 detectable stars against a minimum of 3, so the other tests cannot pass for the wrong reason. Dart: stubbed integrationShortfall to return null (the pre-fix behaviour: nothing rendered) and reran -- 3 of 5 failed. Restored, all green, and the pre-existing session_review_controller_test.dart is still green (17 tests). NOT fixed: the underlying star detector scoring 0 on a frame whose stars an independent peak finder reads at 40 (the verifier's deeper finding). That is a detector-sensitivity question, not a reference-selection one; the fix here makes the pipeline survive it and say so rather than lose the night.
fixes.needs_shared_change: native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/post_session.rs and native/skotiq_native/imaging/src/registration.rs are outside my stated ownership (which covers imaging/src/{integration,master_accumulation,calibration}.rs). No other agent's fix file references either.

fixes.title: Narrowband mixer 'Apply palette' is a dead control: no composite, no file, no error, no log line
fixes.summary: The finding is real but the verifier could not pin the link, and warned not to fix one on faith. I bisected it with a widget test. The panel->callback leg is NOT broken: tapping Apply hands back ('SHO', [[0,1,0],[0,0,1],[1,0,0]]) correctly. What IS broken is that three independent mechanisms made a running, rejected or failing combine indistinguishable from a no-op, which is exactly the reported symptom of pressing it five times and getting nothing. (1) The button was built without isLoading and without disabling, so `combiningNarrowband` was tracked on state and rendered nowhere -- a combine taking tens of seconds looks like an ignored press. Now shows 'Combining...' with a spinner and refuses input. (2) runNarrowband had NO re-entrancy guard, so each extra press launched another concurrent native combine writing to a different stamped path; the runs raced to set narrowbandComposite and the losers left orphaned FITS. Now the re-entrant press returns null. (3) The decisive one: SessionReviewScreen toasts an error string once and remembers it, and runNarrowband's pre-flight guard set the SAME message on every press with no cleared state in between -- so presses 2..N were silent by construction. Verified against the real state sequence: 5 presses produced exactly 1 toast. Fixed on both sides -- the screen resets its memory when the error clears, and runNarrowband clears the error before the guard. The pre-flight message also now names what is actually missing ('3 channels in scope, 1 with a finished FITS on disk') instead of a fixed sentence that cannot distinguish a mis-click from an unmet precondition.
fixes.test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/session_review/narrowband_apply_feedback_test.dart (4 tests: 2 widget tests on the panel incl. the busy state, 1 controller test proving a second press does not start a second native combine via a gated seam, 1 replaying the screen's real toast-dedupe over the observed state sequence)
fixes.caveats: Reverted all three mechanisms and reran: all 3 defect tests failed -- the busy press fired anyway, combineCalls was 2 instead of 1, and the toast replay reported Actual <1> against Expected <5> with the observed sequence [null, <same msg> x5]. Restored; all 4 pass and the pre-existing session_review_narrowband_test.dart is still green. IMPORTANT HONESTY CAVEAT: I could not reproduce the verifier's exact observation (zero narrowband_composites rows after a press in the LIVE app) in a test, because the panel->controller->seam chain is provably intact in-process. If the live failure was the native apiCombineChannels hanging or failing, this change does not make the combine succeed -- but it does make that state visible ('Combining...' with a spinner, and a re-announced error on every retry) instead of presenting as a dead button, which is what the finding is about. Someone with the live rig should re-drive it; the busy state now tells them whether the call is in flight or never started.
